newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, deliveries weigh on Aug.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, deliveries weigh on Aug.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended mixed on Wednesday with nearbys down on news Produce Grain had posted 30 lots of soymeal for delivery against the July and speculation of more deliveries on the way, traders said.
CBOT on Wednesday said 260 lots of soymeal were registered for delivery against the July contract which expired on Tuesday. Open interest in that contract stood at 260 lots as of Tuesday, CBOT said.
Cash soymeal basis levels were weaker on Wednesday, another indication that demand for old crop supplies was weakening, cash brokers said.

Traders also pointed to positioning ahead of Thursday's USDA weekly export sales data and the U.S. Census monthly crush report. Trade sources expected the weekly export sales report to show between 150,000 and 220,000 tonnes of old and new crop soymeal exported as well as 2,000 to 5,000 tonnes of soyoil. They expected the Census report to show soymeal stocks at 255,000 to 298,000 tons and soyoil stocks at 2,125 to 2,150 million lbs.
Soymeal ended $1.00 per ton higher to $0.40 lower with August down $0.40 at $245.30. Soyoil ended 0.08 cent per lb lower to 0.05 cent higher with August down 0.08 at 21.61.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought 200 lots August soymeal and sold 300 August, Continental Grain bought 100 August and LIT bought 100 lots each August and September.
In soyoil, Cargill bought 100 lots each August and September and sold 100 each August and December.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 26,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 24,850. Soyoil volume was pegged at 13,000 lots, against Tuesday's 12,212 lots.
